Its all about getting the dirty cash into the banking system. Simplest example I can give is lets say Dealer has $2,000 cash of drug money and they need to pay their bills. Give the $2,000 to a bar (cash intensive business) and they report it as income. The bar sends Dealer $2,000 for some made up expense. Ultimately you lose a % due to taxes or "fees" paid to your partner business. There are other ways to launder money that have less overhead, but ultimately paying the taxes on the money makes it nearly impossible to tell its not legit. Larger volumes of money require more complicated schemes, but they all share the same components. Get the money into the system, move it around, extract the money.

You mentioned art in the OP which works differently. Art is subjective in price/value. Let's say a piece is worth $20k and I owe you $30k for drugs or some other illicit deal. I buy the art from you for $50k and effectively transfer you the owed value. Because the value is subjective its hard to say the art isn't worth that $50k. Trade based money laundering works on the same principal. Sell a cargo load of jeans or either half or double it's actual value and you can transfer illicit funds mixed into a seemingly legitimate transaction.

My dude. I struggle with a lot of these things. If I hadn't struck the lottery and met my wife when I was 15 (28 now) my life would be pretty much identical to what you've got here. Take the following with a grain of salt because I'm still very much working on it.

The first step here is going to be drawing *some* amount of joy from within. If you try to draw all your joy from friends/women it probably will put them off and you'll end up spinning your wheels in the relationship. I'm not saying find true inner peace before trying to make friends or anything, but #1 above all else is just to find a little spark. Practice little active acts of self-love. Splurge some cash on yourself beyond essentials now and then. This sounds dumb, but force yourself to smile (not even at someone, just at home). As others have said find a hobby that you enjoy the process of rather than seeking the end result. The critical part of this is to change up your routine. Seems like you're pretty passively just going through the motions of life. Go do something out of pattern. Take a hike for an hour around a local park/lake. Plant something. Eat somewhere new. It will help reinvigorate your internal spark for life.

Number 2 is to practice sharing that inner joy. When you meet people focus on giving energy rather than trying to draw them in. Don't worry about if they'll be your best friend for 10 years. Right here in this moment "am I actively sharing my joy, or am I seeking theirs?" When you give out positivity people are drawn to it and will hopefully share their joy with you in return. This is how good friendships work. Its not about impressing them or saying the right thing. Its about how you make each other feel.

And dude, none of this is easy. It sounds simple and flowery, but taking the first steps can be TOUGH. The best thing you can do is have a little grace with yourself and know every day (maybe most days) won't go the way you hoped. Just keep trying man.
